title: app.bin — a 2MB compiled Mach-O binary — is committed to the repo
evidence: git ls-files -s app.bin → "100755 4aaf130a4825b3b67a49e713b76ee83b9e244843 0	app.bin"; file app.bin → "app.bin: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64"; ls -la → "-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 moses staff 2057480 9 Aug 15:47 app.bin"
detail: A platform-specific build artifact is tracked at the repo root (git log shows it added in the 0118cc0/0df9135 commits). The round briefing says: 'The committed `app.bin` (2MB binary) — Verify + flag (likely a blocker-level hygiene issue unless deliberate)'.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached app.bin, add app.bin to .gitignore (bin/ is already ignored), and commit the removal in this PR. The game builds via `odin build app -out:bin/app`.

title: T2 failure path double-frees Odin temp-allocator memory — harness SIGABRTs on a pixel mismatch
evidence: line 138: "out := make([]rl.Color, n, context.temp_allocator)"; line 148: "dimg.data = raw_data(out)"; line 154: "rl.UnloadImage(dimg)". Reproduced: flipping one pixel of a golden PNG then `harness run boot` → "Abort trap: 6" (SIGABRT, exit 134) after goldens/_reports/boot/latest/01000ms/{actual,expected,diff}.png + diff.json were written; the FAIL line and exit 1 never happen.
detail: dimg.data is Odin temp-arena memory (3.7MB, above the temp backing buffer, so it is a fallback-allocator block). rl.UnloadImage frees it via RL_FREE, and free_all(context.temp_allocator) frees the same block at demo end — double free, aborting the exact path §10.5 exists for.
recommended_fix: Own the diff-pixel buffer with the default allocator (make(..., context.allocator)) and delete() it after ExportImage instead of wrapping it in an rl.Image; or skip UnloadImage entirely and free the slice yourself.

title: `harness save` silently blesses demos whose intents/expectations FAILED — exits 0
evidence: line 336: "return ok || save". Save branch: "if save { fmt.printf("  save %-20s ticks=%d captures=%d\n", name, len(hashes), len(demo.capture_frames)) }". Reproduced: appending "expect event run_won within 0ms..1ms" to boot.dem then `harness save boot` printed "save boot ticks=50 captures=1" / "harness: blessed 1 demo(s)" and exited 0, rewriting boot.t1 + the golden.
detail: fail_msgs (intent errors, missed expectations, capture audit) are evaluated in save mode but never printed and never counted — a broken demo's goldens get re-blessed as truth with no warning, defeating the 'deliberate re-bless' contract (spec §10.6).
recommended_fix: In save mode, print fail_msgs and refuse to write the manifest/goldens when fail_msgs is non-empty (return ok, not ok || save); bless only demos whose contract still holds.

title: Replay gate hardcodes the six-node fixture — `map bare` demos would falsely fail it
evidence: line 118-120: "bar := false" / "_ = bar" / "replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(len(live_hashes)), false, &fails)"; line 155: "replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(man.ticks), false, &fails)" (standalone `harness replay`). demo_parse.odin accepts "map bare" as a fixture.
detail: verify_replay and run_replay always pass bare=false, so a bare-fixture demo replays against the six-node bootstrap map — initial state differs, so T1 hashes diverge at tick 1 and the gate fails. Latent: all 7 committed demos use demo_six_nodes.
recommended_fix: Thread the demo's map_fixture into verify_replay/run_replay (read it from the demo file or manifest) and pass bare=true for bare demos; delete the dead `bar` placeholder.

title: Captured T2 frames render the HUD — spec §10.4 says 'the harness renders the world pass only'
evidence: line 28-29: "rl.BeginDrawing()" / "rnd.draw_world(v, &rc.snapshot, mg, time_ms, {}, {})" / "rnd.draw_hud(v, &rc.snapshot, rnd.Hud_State{hint = "", onboarding = false, time_ms = time_ms})". Spec §10.4: 'HUD/debug overlays, wall-clock text, or any non-virtual-time content are excluded from captured frames (the harness renders the world pass only)'.
detail: The HUD is rendered into goldens, deviating from the spec's world-pass-only rule. Not a determinism breach — time_ms is virtual-clock derived and the state is deterministic — but goldens now pin HUD pixels (meter, time) beyond the spec'd scope.
recommended_fix: Either drop the draw_hud call to match §10.4, or amend the architecture note to include the virtual-time HUD pass in the golden scope deliberately — both are one-line changes.
